_comment: Hand-maintained test matrix. Maps each renderer/client to your real-world test status. Edit freely, then rerun: python scripts/gen_compatibility.py. Status is shown verbatim; use 'Tested', 'Partial', or 'Not yet tested'.

esp32_bin.hardware: Waveshare 13.3" Spectra 6 (ESP32-S3-WROOM-2) + Waveshare 7.3" PhotoPainter (ESP32-S3) + Seeed reTerminal E1002 and E1004 (Spectra 6) + Seeed XIAO 13.3" ePaper EE02 (Spectra 6) via tesserae-device-firmware
esp32_bin.notes: Primary daily driver, battery-powered, deep-sleep. The 13.3" client lives at tesserae-device-esp32-bin; the 7.3" PhotoPainter client at tesserae-device-photopainter-7.3-bin. Both pair with the same renderer; the panel preset (waveshare_e6_13_3 vs waveshare_photopainter_7_3) selects the firmware-native row stride. The reTerminal Spectra 6 SKUs consume the same 4-bpp packed frames through tesserae-device-firmware.

esp32_gray_bin.hardware: Seeed reTerminal E1003 (10.3" 1872x1404, 16-level grayscale) running tesserae-device-firmware; also targets the M5Stack PaperS3 (4.7" 960x540), not yet tested
esp32_gray_bin.notes: Confirmed end-to-end on the bench, including GT911 touch input round-tripping through the tap pipeline. The 4-bpp nibble-packed frame (1314144 bytes) is fetched over REST and painted with no on-device decode. The PaperS3 shares this renderer at a different geometry and is awaiting a first bring-up on real hardware.

pi_bin.notes: Fastest Pi path, packed buffer written straight to inky's _buf.

pi_png.notes: Works on every inky-supported panel; quantises on the Pi each frame.

esp32_bw_bin.hardware: Xteink X4 (GDEQ0426T82 / SSD1677, 800x480 mono) running CrossInk with Tesserae client support + Seeed reTerminal E1001 (800x480 mono) running tesserae-device-firmware
esp32_bw_bin.notes: 1-bpp packing confirmed end-to-end: a 48000-byte frame fetched and painted on the panel with no on-device decode, upright in the portrait_flipped composition. The X4 is an e-reader, so the dashboard is its sleep screen rather than a wake-cycle refresh. The remaining Seeed 800x480 mono SKUs (XIAO ePaper 7.5", EE04 7.5") and the Waveshare 4.2" share this renderer but are still unconfirmed.

trmnl_png.hardware: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite 2 (jailbroken) via KOReader trmnl-display plugin + Seeed TRMNL 7.5" OG DIY Kit (XIAO 7.5" panel running the TRMNL firmware)
trmnl_png.notes: 1-bit greyscale PNG fitted to the panel + dithered server-side. The TRMNL X is supported but not yet confirmed here.

esp32_gray2_bin.hardware: Xteink X4 (SSD1677, 800x480) and Xteink X3 (UC8279d, 792x528), both running CrossInk with Tesserae client support + Seeed reTerminal E1001 (4-gray mode) running tesserae-device-firmware + Seeed reTerminal Sticky (SSD1677, 480x800 portrait) running tesserae-device-firmware
esp32_gray2_bin.notes: 4-level grayscale confirmed end-to-end: the 2-bpp frame is fetched and composited as a base frame plus LSB/MSB planes, with distinct grey levels. Packing is byte-identical to the firmware's own 2-bpp bitmap reader, so no decode step is involved. Notable that this works on the X3's UC8253/UC8279d silicon as well as the UC8179-class panels the renderer was written for. The Sticky packs the same 96000 bytes at a portrait 120-byte stride because its firmware transposes on the device; only the stride distinguishes it from the E1001.

circuitpython_bmp.hardware: Raspberry Pi 3 + Waveshare 7" 1024x600 HDMI touch display, and Raspberry Pi 5 + Pi Touch Display 2 (10.1"), both running the community CircuitPython client under PyGame
circuitpython_bmp.notes: Confirmed on Pi-class hardware via the displayio PyGame emulation, pairing through the v1 REST discover flow as circuitpython_generic and painting the uncompressed indexed BMP with no zlib step. Held short of Tested because the microcontroller path the renderer was written for (Pico W class boards decoding via adafruit_imageload) is still unverified. Client: https://github.com/bablokb/tesserae-device-circuitpython
